name: Taming the Beast
summary: In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the last trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, the hunter tames a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion.

sections.title: Mastery of the Canopy
sections.body: Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil to finish their basic beastcraft. After facing beasts of the underbrush, they meet the spirit of the skies: the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod.

sections.title: A Hunter's Bond
sections.body: Taming the Strigid Screecher completes the ancient lessons in communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. The apprentice returns the spent rod to Dazalar, and the training exercises end. Then the hunter gains the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

faq.answer: Strigid Screechers roost in the woods west of Dolanaar. Hunters seek these predatory birds among the canopy and roots outside the village to test their rod.

Dazalar is a night elf hunter trainer in Dolanaar. He guides young kaldorei who have learned basic archery and tracking. He tests them against beasts of land and sky before granting them the ability to bind a real animal companion.

faq.q: Do I get to keep the Strigid Screecher as my pet?
faq.answer: No. The Strigid Screecher tamed during this trial is bound only temporarily by the Taming Rod’s magic. When the trial ends, the hunter surrenders the rod and learns to tame a permanent companion of their own choosing in the wild.

faq.q: What happens after completing this trial?
faq.answer: Dazalar unlocks your ability to tame, call, and dismiss beasts for good. He points you toward further training in Darnassus, where you can learn to feed your companion and teach it to fight.

faq.q: Why do night elves tame owls specifically?
faq.answer: Owls and other birds of prey hold deep cultural meaning for the kaldorei as vigilant hunters of the night and trusted scouts. Mastering a creature of the skies proves you understand aerial predators as well as beasts on the ground.

faq.q: Can hunters choose any animal after this quest?
faq.answer: Yes. Once you gain the ability to tame beasts permanently, you can seek any tameable creature of land, water, or sky across Teldrassil and beyond.

angles.text: As a hunter, this rite marks the passage from fighting alone to forging a lifelong bond with a wild companion.
As a night elf, taming Teldrassil’s native wildlife follows the kaldorei path of living in harmony with nature, rather than bending it through force.
